findings.title: SCHEMA: audit_events has no dedicated actor column; subject overloaded for both tool name and owner identity
findings.description: audit_events.subject is the only identity column. Production code uses it for two incompatible purposes: (a) tool name in wechat-inbound-butler.ts:583 subject=String(def.name) for fatigue decisions, and (b) owner identity in 10+ sites like memories.ts:185 subject="owner", documents.ts:149 subject="owner", project-knowledge.ts:124 subject="owner", traces-procedures-tasks.ts:100 subject="owner", memories-rollback.ts:142 subject="owner". listRecentAuditEvents filters by eq(auditEvents.subject, actor) (runtime-store.ts:626) — which means a tool-name subject like "write_file" matches "write_file" but the same column is treated as the owner actor. This is the D71 first-class SO-001 carry-forward. AuditFatigueReaderOptions.actor was added in D70 T3 but the schema wasn't migrated.
findings.evidence: packages/persistence/src/schema.ts:173-194 (auditEvents def — only subject, no actor); runtime-store.ts:163-218 (appendAuditEventInTx stores subject as the overloaded field); runtime-store.ts:614-637 (listRecentAuditEvents filters by subject column); 10+ owner-routes sites use subject="owner" verbatim; apps/api/src/owner-routes/memories.ts:80 subject: body.subject ?? "owner" (attacker-controlled path).
findings.fix_hint: Migration 0014: ALTER TABLE audit_events ADD COLUMN actor text; populate actor = subject when audit is owner-action, NULL when tool-action; CREATE INDEX audit_events_actor_idx ON audit_events (actor, created_at). Thread actor through all 30+ emit sites. The store contract already has actor as a logical concept (listRecentAuditEvents takes actor filter) — formalize it.

findings.title: SEC-6 path traversal: isAllowedOutboundMediaPath uses resolve() not realpathSync() — symlinks within allowed root bypass the allowlist
findings.description: isAllowedOutboundMediaPath calls resolve(isAbsolute(path) ? path : resolve(process.cwd(), path)) then string-compares to allowed roots. The resolve() does NOT follow symlinks (string-only), but readFile() later (line 94) DOES follow symlinks. So a symlink like /workspace/innocent.txt → /etc/passwd passes the string check (innocent.txt is in workspace), and readFile returns /etc/passwd contents. The dedicated Telegram/Slack media paths share the same channel. This is the SEC-6 pre-scoped D71 item.
findings.evidence: apps/api/src/channel-outbound-media.ts:60-77 (resolve-only check); apps/api/src/channel-outbound-media.ts:92-95 (readFile follows symlinks); apps/api/src/workspace-tools.ts:91-116 (contrast — resolveUnderWorkspace uses realpathSync for correct symlink handling, demonstrating the asymmetry).
findings.fix_hint: Mirror workspace-tools.ts:resolveUnderWorkspace — call realpathSync on the resolved path and compare against realpath's of the roots. ESM/IDS: open(2) with O_NOFOLLOW then read via fd if symlink-safety is preferred over realpath.

findings.title: SEC-3/SEC-8 SSRF: MCP HTTP/SSE transports fetch arbitrary URL with no allowlist or DNS-rebinding guard
findings.description: makeMcpHttpTransport.fetchFn(config.url, ...) and the SSE sibling (sse-transport.ts:69) call user-configured URLs with no validation against validateNetworkAllowlist (packages/domain/src/governance/network-allowlist.ts:74). Approval-runtime uses validateNetworkAllowlist for run_command network scopes, but MCP HTTP/SSE never goes through that gate — a malicious or misconfigured manifest URL pointing at http://10.0.0.1/admin or http://169.254.169.254/ (cloud metadata) would be fetched. envAllowPrivateEgress (BUTLER_V5_SANDBOX_ALLOW_PRIVATE_EGRESS) is not consulted either. Pre-scoped SEC-8/SEC-3.
findings.evidence: packages/adapters/src/mcp/http-transport.ts:44 — config.url is fed directly to fetchFn; packages/adapters/src/mcp/sse-transport.ts:69 — same; packages/runtime/src/approval-runtime.ts:235-237 — the only place validateNetworkAllowlist is invoked (run_command scope); packages/domain/src/governance/network-allowlist.ts — the validator exists but is not wired into MCP transports.
findings.fix_hint: In makeMcpHttpTransport + makeMcpSseTransport: resolve host from config.url via new URL(...).hostname; call validateNetworkAllowlist([`${host}:443`], { allowPrivateEgress: envAllowPrivateEgress(env) }) at construction time; reject construction with a typed error when validation fails.

findings.title: SEC-16 missing HTTP security headers (CSP/HSTS/X-Content-Type-Options/X-Frame-Options/Referrer-Policy/Permissions-Policy)
findings.description: Hono app has only ONE app.use(*) middleware — the bodyLimit check (lines 38-53). No Content-Security-Policy, no Strict-Transport-Security, no X-Content-Type-Options, no X-Frame-Options, no Referrer-Policy, no Permissions-Policy headers. When the API is bound to a non-loopback host (or accessed via a reverse proxy), missing headers expose the WS push endpoint + owner API to MIME-sniffing, clickjacking, and downgrade attacks. Pre-scoped SEC-16.
findings.evidence: apps/api/src/index.ts:38-53 — only bodyLimit middleware; grep across apps/api/src/ for csp|strict-security|x-content-type|x-frame|referrer-policy|permissions-policy returns zero hits.
findings.fix_hint: Add app.use('*', async (c, next) => { await next(); c.header('Content-Security-Policy', "default-src 'self'; frame-ancestors 'none'"); c.header('X-Content-Type-Options', 'nosniff'); c.header('X-Frame-Options', 'DENY'); c.header('Referrer-Policy', 'strict-origin-when-cross-origin'); c.header('Permissions-Policy', 'camera=(), microphone=(), geolocation=()'); if (process.env.HTTPS) c.header('Strict-Transport-Security', 'max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains'); })

findings.title: SEC-5/SEC-11 Slack events: url_verification challenge has no rate limit; team_id allowlist absent
findings.description: /v1/channel/slack/events accepts url_verification (line 344) without any rate limit. Every challenge response does verifySlackSignature HMAC work, but the gateway can still be hammered with valid-signature url_verification challenges at Slack's discretion (network-reachable attacker who learns the signing secret via leak). Also no validation that parsed.team_id (Slack workspace) is in an allowlist — a leaked signing secret lets any Slack workspace wire events to this endpoint. Pre-scoped SEC-5/SEC-11.
findings.evidence: apps/api/src/routes.ts:316-393 — Slack events handler; routes.ts:333-343 — url_verification short-circuits BEFORE signature check (correct for onboarding but unbounded); packages/adapters/src/slack/slack-protocol.ts:49-104 — parseSlackEventPayload does NOT return team_id.
findings.fix_hint: Add a per-IP token-bucket on the challenge branch (1/s during onboarding, 10/day after); thread team_id through parseSlackEventPayload and reject when BUTLER_V5_SLACK_ALLOWED_TEAM_IDS env var is set + team not in list. Owner sees honest 'workspace not allowed' instead of accepting events for unknown teams.

findings.title: SEC-14 interpretQrStatus returns bot_token as plain string — should be Secret<T> branded type
findings.description: QrStatusAction.confirmed.token: string — the bot_token (iLink credential) is just a string field. No branding to flag it as a secret, so logging it (or storing it in env/config) is type-permitted. The Secret<T> wrapper pattern is documented in web/security.md and ECC. Pre-scoped SEC-14.
findings.evidence: packages/adapters/src/wechat/ilink.ts:197-227 — QrStatusAction.confirmed branch returns token as plain string; grep for Secret< across the repo shows zero usages — pattern not yet adopted anywhere.
findings.fix_hint: Define `export interface Secret<T> { readonly __brand: 'Secret'; readonly value: T }` in domain/ports; declare `token: Secret<string>` on QrStatusAction.confirmed; add `unsecret(s: Secret<string>): string` for env-write. Adoption forces compile-time awareness at every consumer (ilink-config.ts: env['WECHAT_TOKEN'] must be wrapped when seeded).

findings.title: Validation: body.subject ?? 'owner' threads attacker-controlled string into audit_events.subject without allowlist
findings.description: POST /v1/owner/memories + 6 sibling endpoints accept body.subject as the audit subject (memories.ts:80,146; documents.ts:68,105; approvals-runs.ts:77,112; traces-procedures-tasks.ts:142,168). The ownerAuthorized middleware requires loopback, so the threat model is local — but a localhost user can put any string into body.subject (e.g. arbitrary UUID, path traversal-looking value, or another owner's id) and the value lands verbatim in audit_events.subject. Combined with D71-CQ-009 (subject = actor column), this is a real audit-trail-spoofing surface. No allowlist/sanitization.
findings.evidence: apps/api/src/owner-routes/memories.ts:80 (subject: body.subject ?? "owner"); apps/api/src/owner-routes/documents.ts:68,105; apps/api/src/owner-routes/approvals-runs.ts:77,112; apps/api/src/owner-routes/traces-procedures-tasks.ts:142,168; apps/api/src/owner-routes/mcp.ts:106 (also body.subject).
findings.fix_hint: Use a resolveActorFromContext(c) helper that reads the loopback address or owner claim and ignores body.subject for audit purposes. If the API must accept a custom subject for delegation flows, allowlist to a regex (e.g. /^[a-z0-9_-]{1,64}$/).
